name: Molten Metal
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free fragment shader shades a churning noise height field as polished metal with glowing heat pools, giving hero panels a dramatic industrial backdrop, with a static CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

metal.description: Surface metal tint, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback.

glow.description: Heat glow colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; white-hot cores are mixed in automatically.

speed.description: Churn speed; 0 holds a still frame.

scale.description: Ripple density; larger gives more, smaller ripples.

heat.description: How much of the surface glows; 0 is cold polished metal.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged.
The surface has bright specular glints and hot spots, so text on it needs a scrim or panel to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo sets its copy on a dark translucent panel).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback drift and shows one still frame of the surface.
Forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText with a visible border.
